record.deltaSub: Starter / Pro survey responses per year
record.headline: Synthesia raised its yearly survey response allowance from 42 to 150 on Starter and from 205 to 720 on Pro, as part of its credits-based usage overhaul.
record.who: Starter and Pro subscribers; the page does not say whether existing customers are treated differently.
record.read: Survey responses are cheap to serve compared with video generation, so loosening them looks like a low-cost way to soften reaction to the credits overhaul while Synthesia keeps tuning where its ceilings bite.
record.caveat: Figures come only from PricingSaaS. Our own capture this week recorded a different survey-response change (350 → 100 credits), so the two records should be reconciled. The same page update also split pricing into individual and business tabs and hid Enterprise from the default view.

record.headline: Shopify introduced Tax managed by Shopify with a new percentage-based tax calculation fee of 0.35% on Basic, Grow and Advanced and 0.25% on Plus, charged after an introductory discount.
record.who: Merchants on Basic, Grow, Advanced and Plus using the Tax managed by Shopify option; a Self-managed tax mode option was added to the same table.
record.read: Tax calculation now looks like a metered line on top of the monthly plan price rather than part of it, a different lever from the plan-price moves Shopify made in October.
record.caveat: The page does not say what the percentage is applied to, how long the introductory discount lasts, or whether the fee applies to existing merchants. That tax calculation had no fee before is inferred from the row being new.

record.headline: Devin's Teams plan dropped its $40 per-month fee for each full developer seat and now costs a flat $80 per month.
rows: Teams, per full dev seat per month
record.who: Teams plan customers; the saving grows with each full developer seat.
record.read: Removing the per-seat charge makes Teams spend predictable and no team pays more than before. It sits oddly with the user cap Cognition cut a week earlier, so the plan is still being reshaped.
